- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3%.
- If model forecast mean is significantly below true outcome mean (e.g., >3% gap over 10+ days), apply mean reversion bias: shift forecast toward historical 30-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >1.5% avg daily gain), model often lags; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
